title: Disk window, file clipboard, Standard File dialog, associations
summary: This is the most mature subsystem in the review. A file manager, a chooser, a file clipboard and an association layer share one browser, one listing store per window and one copy engine. Refusal paths are real and hostile on-disk input is bounded where it is read. The 2026 merges (the chooser becoming a Disk window, the listing-home change, the clipboard folding into one step machine) left very little duplication. The weak spot is the seam those merges created: a Disk window's listing claim is now the mount's write destination, named by [dsk_dseg], and the two memory mechanisms that can take or move that claim mid-mount were not both taught about it. On kern_small a shed inside the mount (the read-ahead window's or the FAT window's claim at step 2, before the listing is written) can hand the destination to the claimant, which can corrupt the FAT window (files-1). On kern_big fm_reloc skips the record being launched, so a compaction inside fm_kinit's first mount leaves FS_VSEG stale and fmv_store copies into the old segment (files-2). Each fix is about ten bytes, and the second saves bytes. Beyond those: the Save box commits names dskw_name83 refuses, the global purge-floor word is clobbered and lifted by unrelated parties, fm_measure is needlessly slow, and a lot of text is stale. SPEC.md 22's preamble and field table, 22.6.3's claim list and 54.0/54.1 still describe the global listing snapshot that 22.6.3 retired.

strengths.title: The chooser IS a Disk window
strengths.why: One browser, painter and line editor; the dialog is hooks raised at named sites behind one resident compare. -1,750 resident bytes when it landed, and every Disk window got the chooser's keyboard selection. The pattern to copy wherever a dialog is a role of an existing window.
strengths.evidence: fdlg.inc header; files.inc:636-643 (fm_kinit adopts [fdlg_win]=0FFFFh); fdlg_hook at fdlg.inc foot

strengths.title: Posted answer, reaped next pass
strengths.why: Ending a modal inside its own callback while the caller is about to draw that window is the classic use-after-destroy. Posting [fdlg_act] and closing in fdlg_reap with the lock taken fresh is Windows' PostMessage(WM_CLOSE)-not-DestroyWindow discipline. fdlg_gate's ZF/CF answer lets both filters freeze input between post and reap without tests of their own.

strengths.title: Cheap guard on the caller's side of a boundary
strengths.why: A per-pass hook that answers no 99% of the time costs one compare, not a far call (measured 1.12% of the machine before). The general rule in SPEC.md 38.1.1 deserves promotion to SPEC.md 1.

strengths.title: Remembered folder per application
strengths.why: Mac System 6 Standard File kept ONE folder in low-memory globals (SFSaveDisk/CurDirStore), so one app's dialog moved every app's default. os8088's per-instance side table does not.

strengths.title: Clipboard as a name; stackless tree walk; a paste that can suspend
strengths.why: An attacker-shaped tree cannot overflow a 384-byte task stack, and the Replace question is a trip through the event loop with all state in .bss. A same-volume Cut is a three-sector relink.

strengths.title: Copies keep compression without knowing about it
strengths.why: The read is raw and the write derives the hint from the bytes, so a packed file arrives packed on both builds with no special case in the engine.

strengths.title: Coherence without I/O
strengths.why: fmv_bcast re-aims dsk_dest at the acting window's claim and block-copies into every other window on that folder instead of re-mounting. A paste repaints one damage union, never wm_paint_all.

strengths.title: Hostile input bounded at the read
strengths.why: ASSOC.DAT counts, sector count and table extent are checked against the file's own size before anything is parsed; header declaration counts are capped; I_SPTR is bounded into fm_pool before use.

strengths.title: One layout cache for painter and hit-tester
strengths.why: fm_layout computes every coordinate once, with field order asserted, so a click and a paint cannot disagree.

findings.title: kern_small: a shed during a loud mount can give the listing's own destination to the read-ahead or FAT window
findings.detail: fmv_load aims dsk_dest at the window's purgeable FS_VSEG claim (MEM_P_VIEW+slot, MEM_PG_LOW) and then mounts. Inside the mount, at step 2 - after the aim and before step 3 writes the listing - dsk_rah_want (MEM_P_DIRW, HIGH, only when a shed took the read-ahead window) and dsk_fatw_want -> dsk_fatw_claim (MEM_P_FATW, MED) claim, both sized by mem_avail_lvl_x at their own rank so a cheaper cache counts as free. mem_claim's shed-and-retry reaches mem_shed_one, which takes the cheapest record strictly below the claimant's rank (skipping only a dirty FAT window); once the TRIV caches are gone that can be this window's own cache. mem_pg_forget's view row hands it to fmv_demote, which zeroes FS_VSEG, FS_VKB and [fm_vseg] but not [dsk_dseg]. The retrying claim can receive those paragraphs, and step 3 then writes the entries and reference index through mov es,[dsk_dseg] into memory that is free or now the read-ahead or FAT window. FAT-window bytes are written back on the next write to that volume. The MEM_RR_ONE dsk_dseg row covers a move on kern_big, not a shed; SPEC.md 22.6.3's safety argument (and tools/dsegaudit.py) covers only the write window, and its 'one claimer in the whole mount is asc_use' is false. ico_need/asc_use in the harvest have the same exposure for the reference-index writes after them.
evidence: disk.inc:4252 dsk_rah_want at mount step 2; disk.inc:4278 dsk_fatw_want; disk.inc:5991 dsk_fatw_claim
disk.inc:7505-7570 dsk_rah_want sizes by mem_avail_lvl_x MEM_PG_HIGH then mem_claimp_x
memory.inc:384 MEM_P_VIEW at LOW (kern_small); 363 FATW MED; 429 DIRW HIGH
memory.inc:1403-1438 mem_shed_one rank scan, only mem_fatw_dirty skipped
SPEC.md:53470 'The one claimer in the whole mount is asc_use'
findings.recommendation: In mem_shed_one's scan, under %ifdef KERN_SMALL, skip a record whose MC_SEG equals [dsk_dseg] (beside the mem_fatw_dirty skip). Add a soak row that fills a 128KB heap until VIEW caches are the cheapest takeable record, navigates a B: window, and compares the FAT window with the disk; remove the skip and the row should go red.
findings.verify_note: Re-read fmv_load, disk_mount_x steps 2-3, dsk_rah_want, dsk_fatw_want, mem_shed_one, mem_pg_own and fmv_demote. Both step-2 claims run with [dsk_dseg] aimed and before .listing; nothing in mem_shed_one or the view row protects the destination. Requires a prior shed of the read-ahead window or a FAT-window claim on that mount, plus no cheaper cache, so it needs memory pressure - but the outcome is a silent write into another claim. Byte estimate refined to ~10. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: kern_big: fm_reloc does not patch the window being launched
findings.detail: app_launch runs KD_INIT before publishing I_STATE=1 (the record is I_STATE 0 until then, so inst_next skips it entirely). fm_kinit_x claims the cache as MOVABLE with fm_reloc, then mounts through fmv_load (dsk_rah_want, dsk_fatw_want, ico_need and asc_use reach mem_claim and so the compactor; mem_can_move does not look at instance state). fm_reloc patches only I_STATE==1 KIND_FILES records, so after a move the launching window's FS_VSEG keeps the old base while [fm_vseg] (fm_reloc's mirror) and [dsk_dseg] (MEM_RR_ONE) move. fmv_store then sees FS_VSEG != [dsk_dseg] and copies the listing out of the new block into the old segment, which is free or someone else's, and FS_VSEG stays stale for the window's life; on DSK_BIGDIR mem_regrow is handed the stale segment. The Standard File chooser opens through the same path.
findings.recommendation: Walk the FM_NSLOT fm_pool blocks and patch any FS_VSEG equal to the moved base, whoever owns the block. fm_kinit_x zeroes FS_VSEG on reuse, so dead blocks are harmless.
findings.bytes_est: ~-12 .text kern_big (a fixed 5-block walk replaces inst_next and the I_STATE/I_KIND tests)
findings.verify_note: Confirmed as described: inst_next skips I_STATE 0, and KD_INIT runs before the publish store. Corrected only the byte estimate: by instruction count the current walk is ~36 bytes and a push cx / mov si,fm_pool / mov cx,FM_NSLOT / cmp-jne-mov / add si,FS_SIZE / loop walk ~23, so about -12 rather than -3. Needs a compaction inside the first mount, so medium stands.

findings.title: The Save box commits names that dskw_name83 refuses
findings.detail: fm_editkey's text arm bounds the buffer at 12, filters characters through dskw_char_x and refuses a leading or second dot. It does not enforce the 8-character stem or the 3-character extension, and it allows a trailing dot. fdlg_save (Enter and the Save button alike) checks only FS_MOK and a non-empty box, so ABCDEFGHIJ, A.BCDE or ABC. reaches the application, whose write fails FERR_NAME after the dialog has gone. SPEC.md 38.5 claims the box accepts exactly what dskw_name83 stores.
findings.recommendation: In fdlg_save, after the empty test: mov si, fdlg_name / FDX dskw_name83n / jc fdlg_beep. Optionally enforce 8/3 per keystroke in fm_editkey for every naming prompt (+~14).
findings.verify_note: Read both sides; no other check exists between fdlg_save and the callback (fdlg_reap_x's commit only stats the name). The SPEC.md 38.5 sentence is fixed below to describe what the code does today.

findings.title: The single purge-floor word is clobbered by a paste and lifted by anyone
findings.detail: mem_pg_fl is one word (level plus owning task). fcp_paste's multi-file arm overwrites it with the UI task's MED regardless of another task's OSAPI_MEM_FLOOR. fcp_lend and mem_free_rec_x (any instance teardown) set MEM_LVL_TOP unconditionally. If DOS has set a floor and is waiting for its compaction to wake it, a paste or any window close in that gap lifts the floor, and DOS's claim then sheds the read-ahead window it asked to keep. Performance only; kern_big (FM_MSEL, OS88_COMPACT) only.
findings.recommendation: Lift only one's own floor: compare the stamp's task with [sch_cur] in fcp_lend and mem_free_rec_x, and do not set a floor in fcp_paste while another task's floor stands. A per-task floor byte is the structural fix.
findings.verify_note: All four sites read as described; mem_rank_bh applies the floor only for the stamped task, so the clobber is a lost floor, not a wrong refusal.

findings.title: fm_measure stages every entry through a 24-byte far copy on every listing
findings.detail: The Used sum calls fmv_dient per entry: it banks and republishes fm_vp/fm_vseg, does a 16x16 mul and a DSK_DE_STRIDE dsk_copy_seg, all to read two words. That runs on every fmv_load and for every window fmv_bcast refreshes: roughly 40 ms for 300 entries and 130 ms at the 1,024-entry kern_big ceiling, per navigation, on the 8088 (predicted) - against a navigation that already costs at least one ~400 ms int 13h.
findings.recommendation: Walk the cache in place with ES = FS_VSEG, stepping SI by DSK_DE_STRIDE from FV_DOFF+20 and doing add/adc of the size dword (~40 cycles an entry). Keep the existing loop as the fallback when FS_VSEG=0. Take the MartyPC figure in the final pass.
findings.verify_note: The loop is as described and the in-place walk is sound. Severity medium -> low: the predicted saving is a few percent of a navigation whose floor is one ~400 ms disk call, and the figure is arithmetic, not measured.

findings.title: fmv_owner's 'cannot happen' fallback tags the cache as the menu save-under
findings.detail: With [fm_vinst]=0 the kern_big arm owns the cache as MEM_P_MSAVE, a purgeable TRIV tag whose mem_pg_own row names menu_sseg. If the branch is ever taken, a shed zeroes the wrong naming word and leaves FS_VSEG dangling: silent corruption from a defensive path.
findings.recommendation: Use a non-purgeable kernel tag, or refuse the claim (stc) on that branch.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked; the branch is unreachable today (fm_vp_set writes fm_vinst first), so this is latent.

findings.title: The commit's volume put-back ignores a failed mount
findings.detail: fdlg_reap_x's commit calls dsk_chdir_x when the globals moved and never reads CF. Packages re-enter their own folder through inst_vol_enter, but the kernel requesters with no instance (drv_dlg_done_x, fm_img_done_x, compress's Uncompress To, DISKOPS's clone-to-image) then act wherever the failed mount landed (the root, with the write gate shut).
findings.recommendation: On CF, skip the callback with a beep, the same way the staleness triple skips it.
findings.verify_note: Read .commit: FDX dsk_chdir_x then .here with no jc.

findings.title: Opening a chooser ends other windows' prompts without repainting them
findings.detail: fdlg_open_x's .endp loop clears modes 1-2 in every pool block so the chooser can own fm_ebuf. Those windows keep drawing 'New folder: ...' or 'Rename ... to:' with no editor behind it until something repaints them, both during the dialog and after.
findings.recommendation: Mark each cleared block FS_DIRTY=FSD_PIXELS (fm_focus spends it as a redraw), or call fm_owed.
findings.verify_note: Read .endp: a byte store and nothing else.

findings.title: Modality filters presses, not drops
findings.detail: A drag that starts inside the chooser belongs to the chooser (fm_onclick's row path reaches fm_drag with no chooser test), and fm_dgdrop resolves the drop with wm_hit. So a file dragged out of a Save chooser moves into a Disk window behind it, or becomes a desktop shortcut through OS88_SHORTCUTS' .desk, while the system is supposedly input-modal.
findings.recommendation: In fm_dgdrop, when [fdlg_win] is non-zero, refuse any target window that is not the chooser.
findings.verify_note: The FM_MSEL test at 3733 only skips multi-select in the chooser; fm_drag is still reached.

findings.title: kern_small keeps a closed window's 2KB cache claimed
findings.detail: The cache is owned by MEM_P_VIEW+slot, which no teardown reaps, so it is freed only when the next tenant of that pool block runs fm_kinit_x. Every closed Disk window, and the chooser's block after every dialog, leaves its claim standing in a heap of about 31KB. The claim is purgeable, but it fragments the heap until shed, and shedding it calls fm_owed for a dead block.
findings.recommendation: Free the chooser's cache in fdlg_reap_x after app_close_win, and a KIND_FILES cache on close.
findings.verify_note: fm_kinit_x's own comment says 'A window that closed left its claim standing'.

findings.title: The empty-icon test ORs 64 bytes per row
findings.detail: fm_draw_icon16 ORs all 32 words of the staged icon to decide 'no icon': about 1,500 cycles a row on the 8088 (or r16,[si+bx] + two dec + jns, x32) and ~3 ms a ten-row list paint (predicted). The fact is known earlier: dsk_ico_stage reaches its .none arm for ICO_R_NONE and for a store row ico_body refuses.
findings.recommendation: Have dsk_ico_stage answer a flag on its .none arm (e.g. CF=1) and test that, instead of scanning the body. Testing the reference byte alone is not equivalent: a row ico_body refuses also stages blank.
findings.verify_note: Corrected the mechanism (ICO_R_NONE is not the only blank case - ico_body's CF also blanks) and the cycle figure (~1,500 a row, not ~800). A genuinely all-zero store body would then draw blank rather than ico_app16; harmless.

findings.title: A folder copy silently skips hidden and system files
findings.detail: fcp_scan asks dsk_dscan with DL=0 and also tests attr 0x0E itself, so a copied folder is short its hidden and system files with no notice. A cross-volume Cut's dskw_rmtree then stops at the first one with FERR_PROT and leaves a split tree. This is XCOPY's default without /H, but the user is not told until the delete half fails.
evidence: disk.inc dsk_dscan header: hidden and system only with DL=1
findings.recommendation: State it in SPEC.md 22.3's limits; optionally toast a count of skipped files before the delete phase.
findings.verify_note: SPEC.md 22.3's 'Two limits' list does not mention it.

findings.title: Any volume's ASSOC.DAT can exhaust the association slots for the session
findings.detail: Nothing frees an association slot in a session. The ASSOC.DAT merge creates an app slot for every app row an extension row names, and assoc_ext_take accepts any first byte above 0x20, including lowercase or high-bit bytes no sanitized display name can match. A crafted or merely large cache fills 16/32 and later real declarations drop silently.
findings.recommendation: Pass the three bytes through dskw_char_x, and stop absorbing a volume's rows when only a few app slots remain.
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked both routines.

findings.title: The inst_tab I_SPTR relocation row covers near pointers as well as segments
findings.detail: mem_rr_tab patches every I_SPTR equal to a moved base. For a built-in kind, I_SPTR is a near pointer into its KD_POOL (fm_pool), not a segment. On kern_big fm_pool is at 0AAFBh (build/kernel.map), above every conventional heap segment, which is the only reason this is safe; a heap that reaches A000h or above (kern_mega's selector values, or a smaller .text) could collide and rewrite a Disk window's state pointer. kern_small does not run the table (no OS88_COMPACT), where fm_pool is at 7D2Dh. Cross-area: recorded for the memory reviewer.
findings.recommendation: Add a %error bounding fm_pool's offset above the highest heap segment, or filter the row by I_KIND.
findings.verify_note: Corrected the offset (0AAFBh on kern_big, not ~0C5xx) and added that kern_small, whose fm_pool is far lower, never runs mem_rr_tab.

findings.title: Three copies of the module far-hop and two macro vocabularies
findings.detail: fdx_go/fdt_go, fcpx_go and extmod's exk_go build the same far frame. FDBODY/FDX/FDK/FDKT/FDRET/FDXJ/FDENT/FDV and FCPBODY/FCPX/FCPXJ/FF/FD/FCV are two dialects of one idea. Each image must carry its own hop, so no resident byte is at stake, but one shared include would make the next module copy nothing.
findings.recommendation: Move the hop and the macro set into one %include (e.g. kernel/modhop.inc), parameterised by the image's section and by how DS is reached (fdlg assumes KERNEL_SEG, filecp loads it under ROM_ADOPT).
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: the two hops are the same frame and differ only in how ROM_ADOPT's segment is fetched.

findings.title: Source shaped around tools that cannot evaluate %ifdef
findings.detail: FDH_RECT exists only because os88ovlchk files fdlg.inc as .modd on both builds and refuses a near call that is legal on kern_big. FDENT is written 'call %1' so the scan cannot see the word. The hops carry STKBALANCE-OK annotations. Teaching the tools to read NASM's preprocessed source per build would let the code say what it means.
evidence: tools/os88ovlchk.py:414,610 skips/does not evaluate the preprocessor
findings.recommendation: Have tools/os88ovlchk.py and tools/stkbalance.py consume nasm -E output (with the build's defines) or the per-build listing.
findings.verify_note: The SPEC text exists and ovlchk's own comment says it does not evaluate the preprocessor.

findings.title: The completion callback could carry the folder
findings.detail: The callback gets the name and must trust that its folder is current, which fdlg_reap makes true with a put-back that does not check its result (files-7). OSAPI_ARG_FILE already answers SI=name, DX=cluster, BL=drive. Passing AH=volume and BX=cluster is additive, since nothing is promised in AH or BX today (AH is 0 at the call), and it makes the folder explicit for kernel requesters.
findings.recommendation: Load AH=[fdlg_sdrv] and BX=[fdlg_scwd] before wm_pkgcall and document it in SPEC.md 38.6 and os88api.inc (abilock --update without a bump).
findings.prior_art: Mac SFReply carried vRefNum with the name
findings.verify_note: AH = 0 at the call confirmed; whether wm_pkgcall delivers BX untouched was not checked.

findings.title: An extension filter for the Open form
findings.detail: Every Open chooser lists everything, and SPEC.md 38.6 tells each app to refuse after the pick. The natural carrier is AH, but fdlg_open_x never reads it (mov ah,0) and the contract defines no AH, so existing packages may leave junk there and adding it needs a bump. Non-matching rows should be greyed rather than hidden, per SPEC.md 47.
findings.recommendation: Add to ABI-BREAK-LIST: AH = a filter (one 3-byte extension pointer or an index of the app's declared extensions); the Open form greys non-matching file rows and refuses them on commit.
findings.prior_art: Mac SFGetFile typeList; Win 3.1 GetOpenFileName lpstrFilter; GEOS file selector token filter
findings.verify_note: fdlg_open_x overwrites AH; neither SPEC.md 38.6 nor the SDK defines it on entry. Not on ABI-BREAK-LIST.

findings.title: System-modal, where COMMDLG was owner-modal and Mac SF app-modal
findings.detail: The chooser freezes every window, the bar and the dock. Owner-modal would be better UX, but SPEC.md 38.2 lists packages that now depend on system modality (Telnet's ZMODEM cancel inference, Artful, RAMDISK, Paint's fsx fence, the image commands).
findings.recommendation: Record only; do not relax without paying for those five dependencies.
findings.prior_art: Win 3.1 COMMDLG disables only the owner; Mac SF ran ModalDialog in a single-app world
findings.verify_note: Record-only.

findings.title: The single 'acting window' context held by discipline
findings.detail: Everything reads [fm_vp]/[fm_vseg]/[fm_vinst] and the fm_lrec mirror published by fm_vp_set; a path that skips it reads the previous window's directory. GEOS passed every method its instance pointer and Windows every WndProc its hwnd. Here the painter uses every register including BP, so the global is the honest choice on an 8088, but it is this subsystem's one invariant held by prose.
evidence: files.inc:946-958 fmv_dient exists to dodge it
findings.recommendation: Record. If the painter is ever restructured, pass the block in DI end to end.
findings.prior_art: GEOS *ds:si instance pointer; Windows hwnd in every WndProc
findings.verify_note: Record-only.

findings.title: ASSOC.DAT is the Mac Desktop file, arrived at independently
findings.detail: A per-volume, OS-maintained icon and association cache, rebuilt when stale, is what the Finder's Desktop file and later Desktop DB were. What the Mac did better was type/creator codes, which bind a document to its program without trusting an extension; FAT has no room for them without sidecars. Compared with Win 3.x's single global WIN.INI [Extensions] table, os8088's defaults plus header declarations plus per-volume cache need no installer and travel with the disk.
findings.recommendation: Record. Keep extensions, since header declarations (54.6) already cover the one file type os8088 owns, as GEOS did with tokens.
findings.prior_art: Mac Desktop file/Desktop DB; Win 3.x WIN.INI [Extensions]/REG.DAT; OS/2 .TYPE extended attributes; GEOS file-header tokens; Amiga .info default tool
findings.verify_note: Record-only.

doc_fixes.old_text: | the Standard File dialog | `MEM_K_FDLG`, `VIEW_KB`, taken at `fdlg_open` | the dialog's |
doc_fixes.new_text: | the Standard File chooser | it IS a Disk window (§38.1): its own `FS_VSEG` claim, taken at `fm_kinit` | the chooser's |
doc_fixes.why: MEM_K_FDLG is reserved and claimed by nothing (memory.inc:254, os88api.inc:2834); the chooser is a KIND_FILES window whose fm_kinit_x runs fmv_fit/fmv_load (files.inc:596-683).

doc_fixes.old_text:
The one claimer in the whole mount is `asc_use`, in the icon
harvest, after the listing is written and sorted, with `ES` already forced to
`LOW_SEG` across it for this exact reason (§66.5.10.2).
doc_fixes.new_text:
It is not the only claimer in the mount. Step 2 claims
after the destination is aimed and before the listing is written:
`dsk_rah_want` (the read-ahead window, if a shed took it) and `dsk_fatw_want`
(a volume's FAT window). The icon harvest claims after the listing is written
and sorted: `ico_need`, and `asc_use` with `ES` already forced to `LOW_SEG`
across it for this exact reason (§66.5.10.2). On `kern_big` a compaction in
any of them moves `[dsk_dseg]` with the block (`mem_rr_tab`'s
`MEM_RR_ONE dsk_dseg` row). On `kern_small` nothing yet stops a shed in any of
them from taking the block itself, because `fmv_demote` zeroes `FS_VSEG` and
`[fm_vseg]` but not `[dsk_dseg]`.
doc_fixes.why: disk_mount_x step 2 calls dsk_rah_want (disk.inc:4252) and dsk_fatw_want -> dsk_fatw_claim (disk.inc:5991) with [dsk_dseg] already aimed by fmv_load (files.inc:1693-1715); memory.inc:3369's comment names ico_need; fmv_demote leaves [dsk_dseg] (files.inc:1408-1437).

doc_fixes.old_text:
Built-in app kind (KIND_FILES), **cap 4** — up to four windows, each on its
own drive and its own folder —
doc_fixes.new_text:
Built-in app kind (KIND_FILES), **cap 5** — up to four of the user's windows
(`fm_count` holds them to `FM_MAXWIN`), each on its own drive and its own
folder, plus the Standard File chooser's (§38.1) —
doc_fixes.why: inst_kinds' Disk row has KD_CAP = VIEW_SLOTS+1 (instance.inc:203); FM_MAXWIN = VIEW_SLOTS bounds the user's windows and FM_NSLOT = FM_MAXWIN+1 (files.inc:424-425).

doc_fixes.old_text:
**The binding rule of this whole section, one sentence: paints read the
window's cache; actions re-sync the global snapshot first.** `disk_dir`,
`disk_icons` and `disk_nfiles` (§18/§19) stay exactly one global mount
snapshot and remain the only thing `loader.inc` and `diskw.inc` ever
resolve a directory index against. Each window additionally owns a
byte-for-byte **copy** of that snapshot in its `VIEW_SEG` slot (§2.3/§22.1),
which is what `W_PAINT`, `fm_layout` and the hit-tester read — so a repaint,
a drag, a raise, a resize or a `wm_paint_all` never touches the floppy. Any
*action* that resolves against the globals (open a package, `dsk_chdir`,
`dskw_mkdir`, and in general every `dskw_*`) first calls `fmv_sync`, which
remounts **only** if the acting window's `(drive, cwd)` differs from
`([disk_drive], [dsk_cwd])` — in the common case, where you act in the
window you last navigated, a compare and a `ret`.
doc_fixes.new_text:
**The binding rule of this whole section, one sentence: paints read the
window's own cache, and a listing mount writes straight into it.** There is
no global listing (§22.6.3): `fmv_load` aims `dsk_dest_x` at the window's
`FS_VSEG` claim, mounts, and aims it back at nothing, leaving `disk_nfiles`
0. That claim is what `W_PAINT`, `fm_layout` and the hit-tester read — so a
repaint, a drag, a raise, a resize or a `wm_paint_all` never touches the
floppy. Any *action* that works on the volume (open a package, `dsk_chdir`,
`dskw_mkdir`, and in general every `dskw_*`) first calls `fmv_sync`, which
re-lists **only** if the acting window's `(drive, cwd)` differs from
`([disk_drive], [dsk_cwd])` — in the common case, where you act in the
window you last navigated, a compare and a quiet `dsk_chdir_q`, which reads
the disk only when the medium could have changed (§18.9.1.2).
doc_fixes.why: disk_dir/disk_icons no longer exist; fmv_load aims dsk_dest_x at FS_VSEG and retires it with dsk_dest_0, zeroing disk_nfiles (files.inc:1693-1771); fmv_sync_x stands with dsk_chdir_q_x when fmv_ishere matches (files.inc:1947-1980).

doc_fixes.old_text:
`disk_icons` is `dsk_nmax` × 64 bytes, already allocated, **already rewritten
every mount** (§18.3 step 4), and a type-0 file's slot was **already all
zero** — the generic-icon sentinel. A document icon composed into that slot
therefore costs **no new per-file RAM and no work in any paint**, and every
consumer of the mount snapshot gets it with no change to a drawing path: both
Disk window views, the per-window view caches (§22.1), and the file dialog
(§38), which reads the snapshot directly because it is modal.
doc_fixes.new_text:
A listing already carries one reference byte per entry (§22.6.3), **already
rewritten every mount** (§18.3 step 4), and a type-0 file's byte was
**already** `ICO_R_NONE` — the generic-icon sentinel. A document icon is
composed into the machine-wide icon store (§25.9) once per association,
keyed by its slot, and the entry's byte names that row, so it costs **no new
per-file RAM and no work in any paint**, and everything that shows a listing
gets it with no change to a drawing path: both Disk window views (§22.1) and
the file dialog, which is a Disk window (§38.1).
doc_fixes.why: disk_icons no longer exists; the mount's pass 4b composes with assoc_compose and keys the store row by [assoc_docslot] (disk.inc:9290-9330), and fmv_get_icon resolves a window's reference byte through dsk_ico_stage (files.inc:990-1010, disk.inc dsk_ico_stage).
